title: 2026 Best K-Drama Filming Locations in Seoul: Your Real Fan Guide

Go beyond the screen: actually visit these K-drama spots

Sure, you can watch Goblin fall in love all over again, but wouldn't it be cooler to stand where he stood? Forget just dreaming about it, let's talk about the K-drama filming locations you can *actually* visit in Seoul. This isn't about tourist traps; it's about places that feel real, places you can find on a map and get to without a film crew.

Seoul's iconic K-drama filming locations

So, you wanna walk the same streets as your favorite leads? I get it. It’s like, a whole other level of connecting with the show. Here are a few spots that are legit visitable and totally worth the subway ride.

Namsan Park & N Seoul Tower

Seriously, who hasn't teared up or swooned here on screen? From 'Boys Over Flowers' to 'My Love from the Star,' this place is practically a K-drama cliché, but in the best way. It's famous for those love locks, obviously, but the whole park has a vibe.

Nearest Station: Myeongdong Station (Line 4), Exit 3. From there, you can take the Namsan Oreumi (a special cable car elevator) or the 01 community bus up. The bus is cheaper, like ₩1,200.
Hours: Park is always open, N Seoul Tower usually 10 AM - 11 PM (check specifics).
Take: Go on a clear day for actual views, or at sunset if you want that dramatic lighting. The locks are... a lot, but it's part of the experience.

Bukchon Hanok Village

This is where you go for that classic, traditional Korean house aesthetic. It's been in SO many dramas, think 'My Mister' or 'Goblin' (yes, again). It’s not just a set; people actually live here, so be respectful, ppl!

Nearest Station: Anguk Station (Line 3), Exit 1 or 2. It’s a short walk uphill.
Hours: Generally accessible during daylight hours. Some cafes/shops have their own hours, usually 10 AM - 5 PM.
Take: Wear comfy shoes. It's hilly. And quiet. Seriously, keep the noise down.

Ewha Womans University Street

Remember those college romance dramas? This street, just outside Ewha Womans University, is basically ground zero for that vibe. 'Weightlifting Fairy Kim Bok Joo' had scenes here, and honestly, it just feels youthful and energetic.

Nearest Station: Ewha Womans University Station (Line 2), Exit 2 or 3.
Hours: The street is always open. Shops and cafes have typical business hours (10 AM - 9 PM).
Take: Lots of cute cafes, cosmetic shops, and fashion boutiques. Good for a chill afternoon wander if you're in the area.

Yeouido Hangang Park

The Han River is a whole character in itself in many dramas. Yeouido is one of the most popular spots, especially for those dramatic riverside scenes, picnics, or even those iconic bike rides. Think 'Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha' or 'Vincenzo' – it’s got that expansive, urban-escape feel.

Nearest Station: Yeouinaru Station (Line 5), Exit 1, 2, 3, or 4. Or Yeouido Station (Line 5 & 9) for other parts.
Hours: Always open. Bike rentals usually 9 AM - 9 PM.
Take: Rent a bike (usually around ₩3,000-₩4,000/hour) and just cruise. Grab some convenience store ramen or fried chicken for the ultimate K-drama picnic.

Planning your K-drama pilgrimage

Okay, so actually hitting these spots requires a bit of strategy, especially if you're trying to do it efficiently. You don't want to spend your whole trip backtracking. A lot of these spots are relatively close to each other, especially the ones in the Jongno/Jung-gu area like Bukchon and Namsan. Trying to map out a route that hits your top drama locations without wasting half your day on the subway can be a headache. Honestly, building a custom itinerary in the AI planner can save you SO much time and stress figuring out the transit between places like this.

FAQ

Q. How do I get around to these K-drama filming locations?
A. Seoul's subway system is amazing. Get a T-Money card (reloadable transit card) and use apps like Naver Maps or Kakao Maps – Google Maps doesn't work as well for transit in Korea. Each location listed has its nearest station.

Q. Are these places actually interesting if I'm not a huge K-drama fan?
A. Totally! Bukchon Hanok Village is beautiful regardless, Namsan offers great city views, and the Han River parks are where locals hang out. The drama connection is just a fun bonus.

Q. Can I take photos at these locations?
A. Yes, generally. Just be mindful in places like Bukchon Hanok Village where people live. Avoid being overly disruptive, especially if filming yourself.

Q. What's the best time of year to visit K-drama filming locations?
A. Spring (cherry blossoms!) and Autumn (fall foliage) are gorgeous and feature in many dramas. Summer can be hot and humid, while winter can be cold but has its own dramatic charm.
